observations.observation_key: projsayre/sayre|SEC-10|secrets-audit-data-lifecycle|scripts/ledger-append.mjs's --inline/--lite/--re-gate/--hotfix mutual-exclusion and composition handling (PL-12 new surface)|v8-inline-lane-composition
observations.target_asset: scripts/ledger-append.mjs's --inline/--lite/--re-gate/--hotfix mutual-exclusion and composition handling (PL-12 new surface)
observations.attempt: Attempted every composition of --inline with the other lane flags to see whether any relaxes a gate or produces an ambiguous/mislabeled entry: --inline --lite, --inline --re-gate, --inline --hotfix (in both flag orders, including placing --inline after --hotfix's --files, which consumes the rest of argv), and --inline with --override-review/--override-security (the one composition the spec says MUST be accepted).
evidence: --inline --lite and --inline --re-gate: both refused (scripts/ledger-append.mjs:1375-1393) before any `.pipeline/` file is read — traced the exact call order in main(): `assertKnownFlags` -> `lite`/`inline` boolean derivation -> `readOverrideReason` x2 (pure argv) -> `readRegateArgs` (pure argv) -> the `if (lite){...}`/`if (inline){...}` mutual-exclusion blocks -> `readInlineArgs` -> ONLY THEN `readReviewJson(pipelineDir)`, the first disk read. Confirmed by the test fixture's own construction (`[inline] --inline --lite and --inline --re-gate are each refused... before any .pipeline/ file is read`): the fixture's `.pipeline/` directory is deliberately empty, so a refusal could only have come from the argv-only checks.

One caveat traced directly (matches review's own Suggestion #2, independently re-derived rather than taken on its word): `--inline --re-gate --ticket X --why-inline Y` WITHOUT `--tester-ran` surfaces readRegateArgs's own "--re-gate requires --tester-ran" refusal (line ~1309) rather than the `--inline --re-gate` mutual-exclusion message, because `readRegateArgs(argv, { inline })` runs (line 1347) before the mutual-exclusion block (line 1375). This still refuses, still before any `.pipeline/` read, and writes nothing — the ONLY effect is which message the caller sees, never a relaxed gate. With the full re-gate arg set (`--tester-ran true --ticket X`), the correct `--inline --re-gate` message fires as documented.

--inline --hotfix: `--hotfix` is dispatched BEFORE main() even runs (`if (process.argv.includes('--hotfix')) runHotfix(...) else main()`), and runHotfix's own `assertKnownFlags(argv, { knownFlags: HOTFIX_KNOWN_FLAGS, ... })` does not include `--inline` in its known-flags set. Traced both orderings: `--hotfix --inline ...` fails immediately with `unrecognized argument "--inline"` (nothing written); `--hotfix ... --files --inline` treats the literal string "--inline" as one more file path in the `--files` list (harmless — `--files` consumes every remaining token verbatim once reached) — in neither ordering does `--inline` invoke any inline-lane logic at all inside a hotfix run.

--inline --override-review/--override-security: traced as the one composition that MUST succeed (not a bypass finding) — confirmed both flags are read via the shared, unconditional `readOverrideReason` (argv-only, before any lane-specific branch) and thread into the SAME `reviewOverridden`/`securityOverridden`/`bypass` logic every other lane uses; independently re-ran `[inline] a non-PASS gate accepted via --override-* composes with the inline disclosure...` this session and read its assertions directly: `bypass: true`, excluded from index.json, `(INLINE) (OVERRIDE)` title, `inline` object intact and unmodified by the override.

observations.attempt: Constructed and traced the worst case the ticket's own spec explicitly calls out as approver-reversible (D-2): a change far past every one of the lite lane's own bounds (file count, changed lines, line length) AND touching a path in the lite lane's own barred-path union (services/core/src/services/**), submitted via --inline, to determine whether the absence of a mechanical size bound on this lane allows a large or security-sensitive change to be indexed WITHOUT security's own scrutiny — the actual attack D-2 could enable, as distinct from the disclosed-but-accepted D-018 test-ordering tradeoff.
evidence: Traced main()'s control flow directly: the `securityJson.verdict !== 'PASS'` gate (scripts/ledger-append.mjs:1441-1447) and `refuseIfStale('security.json', ...)` (line 1439) are UNCONDITIONAL on the non-lite path — `inline` never enters that branch's condition at all (`if (lite) {...} else { securityJson = readSecurityJson(...); ... }`, line 1420). There is no code path by which a large `--inline` change reaches the ledger without security.json showing PASS (or an explicit, disclosed `--override-security`).

Independently re-ran `[inline] a change far past every lite bound — file count, changed lines, line length, and a barred path — is recorded, not refused: the measurement gates nothing` (scripts/ledger-append.test.mjs) this session: a 9-file, >150-changed-line, >2000-char-line change touching `services/core/src/services/technicalTreeService.ts` (in the lite lane's own barred union) still requires a genuine, independently-produced, PASS `security.json`/`security-history/` run to succeed at all (the fixture's `runInline` only succeeds because the fixture also supplies one) — the test demonstrates the size measurement gates NOTHING, but does not, and structurally cannot, demonstrate that security scrutiny itself was skipped, because the harness never lets an inline run reach `entry.json` without a real security PASS in the fixture.

This is a materially different risk shape from SEC-10 v4/v5/v6 (the lite lane's own size-bound gaps): those are exploitable specifically BECAUSE `security` never runs at all on `--lite` — size was the ONLY compensating control, and it was shown to have real gaps. On `--inline`, `security` is unconditional and full regardless of measured size, so "escape scrutiny via size" is blocked at every size, not merely below some threshold.

The residual D-2 leaves genuinely open — tests are written after the diff exists (the D-018 inversion), at any size, with no mechanical bound — is a disclosed, structural property of the lane (`.sdd/pipeline.md`'s /inline-edit "Honest limits" (a), spec.md's D-2, review.md's own "D-2 adjudication" section with its honesty note) and is compensated by `security` genuinely reviewing the change in full, the same compensating control the full, ordinary `/pipeline` lane already relies on for arbitrarily large `dev`-authored diffs today (the full lane also carries no mechanical size bound on `dev`'s own output) — D-2 does not lower this lane's risk profile below what an unbounded, ordinary /pipeline diff already carries; it forgoes only what a bounded /pipeline-lite diff's SKIPPED security stage would otherwise have needed size to compensate for.
